name: Microsoft Azure
scope_notes: Covers Microsoft Azure (Azure Storage, Azure Resource Manager, Microsoft Entra Workload ID, Azure DevOps Services). Azure Storage and ARM controls are per subscription/account; Conditional Access for workload identities needs Workload Identities Premium; Azure DevOps PAT policies need an Entra-backed organization. Entra delegated/app-only OAuth for Graph and managed identities are covered by the separate microsoft platform.

controls.name: Allow storage account key access (AllowSharedKeyAccess = false)
controls.what: Rejects all requests authorized with account keys, including account and service SAS; user delegation SAS still works.
controls.setting: Storage account > Configuration > Allow storage account key access; ARM property allowSharedKeyAccess

controls.name: Azure Policy: Storage accounts should prevent shared key access
controls.what: Audits or prevents storage accounts that permit Shared Key authorization.

controls.name: Regenerate key (RegenerateKey)
controls.what: Replaces an account key and revokes SAS signed with that key.
controls.setting: Storage account > Access keys > Rotate key; POST .../regenerateKey

controls.name: Key expiration policy
controls.what: Shows a reminder and enables Azure Policy compliance checks when keys are not rotated in the interval; does not disable keys.
controls.setting: Storage account > Security + networking > Access keys > Set rotation reminder

controls.name: Storage firewall network rules
controls.what: Limits which IPs, VNets and resource instances can reach the account endpoint.

controls.name: SAS expiration policy (Log / Block)
controls.what: Sets a recommended max SAS interval for service and account SAS; Block denies out-of-policy SAS, default Log allows them.

controls.name: Stored access policy
controls.what: Service SAS bound to a stored access policy can be revoked by changing or deleting the policy.

controls.name: Revoke user delegation keys
controls.what: Revokes all user delegation keys for the account, invalidating every user delegation SAS.

controls.name: Conditional Access for workload identities
controls.what: Blocks token requests by single-tenant service principals from outside named locations or when risky.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Conditional Access > Workload identities

controls.name: App management policy (passwordAddition, passwordLifetime, asymmetricKeyLifetime)
controls.what: Blocks new password secrets or caps secret/certificate lifetimes for new or updated apps.

controls.name: Remove credential / disable service principal
controls.what: Deleting the secret, certificate or federated credential stops new token requests; disabling the SP is a CAE revocation event for Microsoft Graph only.
controls.setting: App registrations > Certificates & secrets; Enterprise applications > Properties

controls.name: Azure RBAC role assignment scope
controls.what: Service principal ARM access is limited to its assigned roles and scopes.

controls.name: Restrict global personal access token creation
controls.what: New PATs must target specific organizations.

controls.name: Restrict full-scoped personal access token creation
controls.what: New PATs must use custom scopes.

controls.name: Enforce maximum personal access token lifespan
controls.what: Caps lifetime of new or renewed PATs in days.

controls.name: Restrict personal access token creation
controls.what: Only allowlisted users (or packaging-only) can create or regenerate PATs; existing PATs keep working.

controls.name: Automatically revoke leaked personal access tokens
controls.what: PATs found in public GitHub repos are revoked automatically.

controls.name: Enable IP Conditional Access policy validation on non-interactive flows
controls.what: Checks Entra IP-based Conditional Access on PAT REST calls.

controls.name: Token Admin revoke authorizations
controls.what: Admins revoke users' PATs by authorization ID; disabling a user also revokes their PATs.

controls.name: Block password addition (passwordAddition restriction)
controls.what: Blocks adding new client secrets to applications and service principals; certificates are not blocked by this restriction.
controls.setting: Entra ID > Enterprise apps > Application policies > Block password addition (or tenantAppManagementPolicy via Microsoft Graph)

controls.name: Users can register applications
controls.what: Set to No so only admins and Application Developer role holders can create app registrations (and so add secrets, certificates or federated credentials to new apps).
controls.setting: Entra ID > Users > User settings > Users can register applications

controls.name: Not allowed resource types (Azure Policy) for userAssignedIdentities/federatedIdentityCredentials
controls.what: Blocks creating federated identity credentials on user-assigned managed identities in a subscription or resource group; does not cover app registrations.
controls.setting: Azure Policy > Definitions > Not allowed resource types > Assign

no_control.what: Key expiration policy only reminds; keys never expire.
Azure does not track issued SAS tokens, so there is no inventory or per-token revoke for account SAS.
CAE for workload identities does not cover Azure Resource Manager; ARM tokens survive SP disable until expiry.
App management policies do not affect existing credentials or token issuance for existing apps.
PAT use (token access) is not recorded in the Azure DevOps audit log.

controls_unknown: Whether Azure Activity Log records the service principal identity for ARM read calls made with azure-3/azure-4 tokens (Activity log typically skips reads).
Exact Entra audit activity name for adding/removing a federated identity credential.
Default of the Azure DevOps "IP Conditional Access policy validation on non-interactive flows" policy.
Maximum Azure DevOps PAT lifetime when no tenant policy is set.
Token format or prefix for storage keys, SAS, client secrets or Azure DevOps PATs.
Whether app management policies require a specific license.

authentication.summary: Two account keys (key1/key2) per storage account; requests are HMAC-SHA256 signed in the SharedKey Authorization header. Keys give full data access and can mint SAS tokens.

federation.details: Shared Key does not use Microsoft Entra ID, so Entra Conditional Access does not apply; docs say Shared Key must be disallowed to protect an account with Conditional Access.

ip_restriction.boundary: Storage firewall network rules (IP, VNet, resource instance, trusted services) apply to requests to the account endpoint; default allows any network.

lifetime.summary: No expiry; key expiration policy only shows a rotation reminder

renewal.summary: Keys stay valid until regenerated; rotate by switching to the second key, then regenerating the first.

administration.summary: Anyone with Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action can read keys. Admins can disallow Shared Key per account (AllowSharedKeyAccess=false) and enforce that with Azure Policy.
administration.conditions: Shared Key is allowed when the property is unset.

sso.details: Docs say Conditional Access protects a storage account only after Shared Key authorization is disallowed.

offboard.details: The two access keys belong to the storage account, not to a user.

inventory.details: Each account has exactly two keys, listed under Security + networking > Access keys or with az storage account keys list (per account).

usage.ui: Storage account > Monitoring > Diagnostic settings: send StorageBlobLogs to a Log Analytics workspace; then Logs: StorageBlobLogs | where AuthenticationType == "AccountKey"; group by AuthenticationHash to tell keys apart

reads.ui: Log Analytics (after diagnostic setting): StorageBlobLogs | where AuthenticationType == "AccountKey" and OperationName == "GetBlob"

kill.ui: Storage account > Security + networking > Access keys > Regenerate (each key); or Settings > Configuration > Allow storage account key access = Disabled
kill.cli: az storage account keys renew --resource-group <rg> --account-name <account> --key primary (then --key secondary); or az storage account update --name <account> --resource-group <rg> --allow-shared-key-access false

log_sources.name: Azure Activity Log
log_sources.notes: Control-plane writes/actions (e.g. listKeys, regenerateKey); 90 days free; reads typically not captured.

log_sources.name: Azure Storage resource logs (StorageBlobLogs)
log_sources.notes: Data-plane requests incl. AuthenticationType and AuthenticationHash; not collected until a diagnostic setting routes them.

credential_id_fields.notes: key1|key2 plus SHA-256 hash of key.

containment.steps: Regenerate the exposed key (and the other if unsure); or set AllowSharedKeyAccess=false.
containment.notes: Regenerating also revokes SAS signed with that key; dependent apps break.

calls.log_notes: StorageBlobLogs only if diagnostic setting configured.

unknown: No whoami call for Shared Key or SAS.

credentials.name: Shared access signatures (SAS): account SAS, service SAS, user delegation SAS

authentication.summary: Signed URL token. Account and service SAS are signed with an account key; user delegation SAS is signed with a user delegation key obtained with Entra credentials (Blob only). Anyone holding the SAS can use it.

federation.details: Account/service SAS rely on Shared Key and bypass Entra; user delegation SAS is authorized with Entra credentials and still works when Shared Key is disabled.

ip_restriction.boundary: Optional signed IP (sip) in the SAS plus the storage firewall; the SAS IP cannot grant access beyond firewall rules.

lifetime.summary: Expiry set by creator; user delegation key max 7 days; SAS expiration policy can Log or Block over-long SAS

administration.summary: SAS tokens are not tracked by Azure. Controls: disallow Shared Key (blocks account/service SAS), SAS expiration policy, stored access policies (service SAS only), revoke user delegation keys, regenerate account keys.
administration.conditions: Stored access policies not supported for account or user delegation SAS.

sso.details: A user delegation SAS is secured with Entra credentials; account and service SAS are signed with Shared Key, which Conditional Access does not cover unless Shared Key is disallowed.

inventory.details: SAS tokens are generated client-side and Azure Storage does not track them.

sso.ui: Storage account > Settings > Configuration > Allow storage account key access = Disabled (leaves only Entra-backed user delegation SAS)

usage.ui: Log Analytics (after diagnostic setting): StorageBlobLogs | where AuthenticationType == "SAS"; AuthenticationHash identifies the SAS

reads.ui: Log Analytics: StorageBlobLogs | where AuthenticationType == "SAS" and OperationName == "GetBlob"

kill.ui: Account/service SAS: Storage account > Security + networking > Access keys > Regenerate the signing key, or change/delete the stored access policy. User delegation SAS: revoke delegation keys

token_format.notes: SAS is a query-string token appended to the resource URL.

log_sources.name: Azure Storage resource logs (StorageBlobLogs)
log_sources.notes: Data-plane requests incl. AuthenticationType and AuthenticationHash; not collected until a diagnostic setting routes them.

containment.steps: Account/service SAS: regenerate signing key or change stored access policy. User delegation SAS: revoke-delegation-keys. Or disallow Shared Key.
containment.notes: User delegation revocation may be delayed by caching.

unknown: Creation of a SAS is client-side and not logged.

calls.log_notes: StorageBlobLogs only if diagnostic setting configured.

unknown: No whoami call for Shared Key or SAS.

credentials.name: Service principal client secrets and certificates (used against Azure Resource Manager)

authentication.summary: App registration secret or certificate used in the client credentials flow to get an Entra access token for Azure Resource Manager; access is set by Azure RBAC role assignments.

federation.details: Not a user sign-in. Conditional Access for workload identities can block by location or risk, but only at token request and only for single-tenant SPs, and needs Workload Identities Premium.

ip_restriction.boundary: Location-based Conditional Access for workload identities blocks token requests from outside allowed ranges. Already-issued ARM tokens are not re-checked (CAE for workload identities is Microsoft Graph only).

lifetime.summary: Secret up to 24 months; access tokens 60-90 min

renewal.summary: Secret or certificate is reused to request new access tokens until it expires or is removed.

administration.summary: App management policies can block new password secrets or cap secret/certificate lifetimes; they do not affect existing apps. Credentials are removed in the app registration; the SP can be disabled.
administration.conditions: Tenant default policy is disabled by default.

sso.details: Conditional Access for workload identities applies to single-tenant service principals only and needs Workload Identities Premium; multitenant apps are not covered.

offboard.details: Client secrets and certificates belong to the application/service principal, not a user.

inventory.details: Each application object exposes its passwordCredentials and keyCredentials collections through Microsoft Graph (GET /applications).

authentication.summary: User-owned token for Azure DevOps REST, Git and package feeds; scoped to one organization (global PATs stop working Dec 1, 2026) and limited to the owner's permissions.

federation.details: PATs must meet Entra sign-in policies on REST calls; IP-based Conditional Access is checked on PAT calls only if the org enables "IP Conditional Access policy validation on non-interactive flows".

ip_restriction.boundary: Enforced on PAT REST calls only with the org policy enabled and an Entra IP-based Conditional Access policy.

lifetime.summary: Expiry chosen at creation; tenant max-lifespan policy; becomes inactive if owner does not sign in within 90 days (Entra-backed orgs)

renewal.summary: Reused until expiry; regenerating issues a new value and invalidates the old one.

administration.summary: Tenant policies: restrict global PATs, restrict full-scoped PATs, max lifespan, auto-revoke leaked PATs (on by default). Org policy: restrict PAT creation with allowlist. Admins can revoke users' PATs via Token Admin API.
administration.conditions: Policies require an Entra-backed organization; restricting creation does not stop existing PATs.

sso.details: Conditional Access MFA applies to web flows only; IP-based policies apply to PAT REST calls only if the org enables IP Conditional Access policy validation on non-interactive flows.

offboard.details: PATs stop working when the account is disabled or removed (up to one hour delay), but are not deleted and work again if access is restored.

inventory.details: Project Collection Administrators can list PATs per user with GET .../_apis/tokenadmin/personalaccesstokens/{subjectDescriptor}; no single org-wide list.
